The Prophet and Jabir prayed in one garment, ends crossed over the shoulders or tied as a waist-sheet if tight, the Prophet asking whether everyone had two garments.
Men prayed with waist-sheets tied at the neck, the Prophet was never again seen naked, Umar listed garment pairs, and two wrappings, certain Muhrim garments and naked Tawaf were forbidden.
Women attended Fajr in sheets; the Prophet sent away a marked garment and pictured curtain distracting his prayer, cast off a silk gown and prayed in a red cloak.
Abu Huraira saw seventy Suffa men without upper garments, in waist-sheets or sheets tied at the neck, which they held lest their private parts be exposed.
Umar urged a silk cloak on the Prophet for Fridays; he said it is worn by one with no share in the Hereafter; Umar gave his to a pagan brother.
Umar urged a silk cloak on the Prophet for Eid; he said it is for those with no share in the Hereafter, then later sent Umar one to sell.
The Prophet sent Umar a silk garment to benefit from by selling, not to wear, since it is worn by one with no share in the Hereafter.
Calling a silk cloak the dress of one with no share in the Hereafter, the Prophet sent Umar one not to wear, and Umar gave it to a pagan brother.
Ali cut up a silk dress the Prophet gave him on seeing his anger, and of a silk cloak from Ukaidir the Prophet said Sa'd's handkerchiefs in Paradise are better.
The Prophet sent Umar a silk cloak not to wear but to sell or give away, and Umar sent it to his brother in Mecca, not yet a Muslim.
Aisha, in a coarse five-dirham dress, says that in the Prophet's time women wishing to look elegant would borrow such a dress from her.
The Prophet allowed Abdur-Rahman bin Auf and az-Zubair to wear silk because of itching from a skin disease or lice, and they wore it in battle.
Umar urges buying a silk cloak for Eid and delegations; the Prophet says it is worn by one with no share in the Hereafter, yet sends Umar one to sell.
Ali wore a silk suit the Prophet gave him, then, seeing anger on his face, cut it up and shared it among his womenfolk.
Allah will not look at one dragging his garment in pride; a proud man sank into the earth; Abu Bakr's slipping Izar was excused; the Prophet once hurried, dragging his.
The Prophet put on his Rida and walked, Zaid and Ali following, to the house where Hamza was, and asked permission to enter.
The Prophet kept a Qaba for Makhrama and took off a silk Farruj after praying in it as unfit for the God-fearing; Anas wore a yellow hooded cloak of Khazz.
The Prophet entered Mecca in a helmet, smiled and gave to a bedouin who yanked his Burd, and gave a woman's Burda to a man wanting it as his shroud.
Hibra, a Yemeni cloth, was the garment the Prophet loved most, and when he died he was covered with a Hibra Burd.
The Prophet sent a patterned Khamisa that distracted him in prayer to Abu Jahm for a plain sheet, and Aisha showed the Kisa and Izar he died wearing.
The Prophet forbade one-garment wraps baring a side or the private parts, and Mulamasa and Munabadha sales; he dressed little Um Khalid in a black Khamisa, wishing her long life.
Silk is forbidden beyond two fingers' width; who wears it here will not hereafter; itch excused Az-Zubair and Abdur-Rahman; Ali's silk went to his wives, Umar's to sell or give.
The Prophet dressed Um Khalid in a Khamisa, forbade men saffron, wore a red suit, and prayed in shoes; put the right shoe on first, and never walk in one.
Abu Bakr said his waist sheet slackened on one side, and the Prophet said he was not among those who drag their garments out of pride.
Umar urged the Prophet to buy a silk cloak for delegations; he said silk is worn by one with no share hereafter, then sent Umar a cloak only to sell.
The Prophet forbade two ways of wearing a garment, Ishtimal As-Samma and Ihtiba leaving the private parts uncovered, and two bargains, Mulamasa and Munabadha.
